name: Negative-Review Rapid-Response

parameters.content:
## Negative-Review Rapid-Response

### How it works

1. The workflow triggers when a new review is received via webhook and normalizes the incoming data.
2. It validates the review and checks for duplicates to ensure only new, valid reviews are processed.
3. Negative reviews trigger the creation and sending of an instant SMS alert to the firm.
4. The workflow generates a draft review response using an AI service and performs a compliance safety check.
5. Finally, it logs the compliance audit and sends an email notification to the firm about the negative review.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Configure the webhook to receive new reviews from your review platform or Zapier.
- [ ] Set up credentials and variables for accessing messaging services like Twilio for SMS alerts.
- [ ] Provide API credentials for the AI service (Anthropic) used for generating draft responses.
- [ ] Configure email credentials for sending notifications to the firm.
- [ ] Ensure n8n workflow static data permissions for duplicate review detection.

### Customization

You can customize alert message content and draft response prompts in the "Build Alert And Draft Prompt" node to better fit your firm's tone and policies.

## Trigger and normalize input

Receives new review data via webhook and normalizes it for processing.

## Validate and deduplicate reviews

Checks review payload validity and filters out duplicates or invalid entries to ensure quality processing.

## Detect negative ratings and skip positives

Determines if reviews are negative and filters out positive reviews with no further action.

## Build and send alerts

Creates alert messages and draft prompts then sends instant SMS notifications to the firm.

## Generate response and notify firm

Generates AI draft responses, conducts compliance checks, logs audits, and emails the firm about negatives.

nodes.name: When New Review Received Webhook
nodes.notes:
Receives each new review from your Zapier 'New Review' zap.

Zapier setup: Zapier (free tier works) → Create Zap → Trigger app 'Google Business Profile' → Trigger event 'New Review' → connect your Google account and select your location → Action app 'Webhooks by Zapier' → Action event 'POST' → paste this node's Production URL → Payload Type: json.

In the Zapier action's data mapping, use these exact field names so the next step can read them:
  review_id — the review's unique ID
  reviewer_name — the reviewer's display name
  star_rating — the star rating (Zapier passes Google's word form: ONE/TWO/THREE/FOUR/FIVE)
  review_text — the review comment
  review_url — link to reply to the review (if Zapier doesn't offer one, leave blank — the fallback FIRM_GBP_DASHBOARD_URL Variable is used instead)
  location_name — your business location name (only needed if you manage more than one)
  created_at — when the review was posted

Any reputation tool that can POST JSON (Podium, BirdEye, etc.) can point here directly instead of using Zapier, as long as it sends the same field names.

nodes.name: Parse New Review Data
nodes.notes:
Reads the review Zapier sent and prepares it for the negative-review check.

Expects the exact field names from your Zapier 'Webhooks by Zapier' POST action — see the deploy guide's Zapier setup for the mapping screen: review_id, reviewer_name, star_rating, review_text, review_url, location_name, created_at.

star_rating accepts either a number (1-5) or Google's word form (ONE..FIVE) — Google Business Profile's own API returns the word form, so Zapier's raw field passes it through that way; this node converts either.

Output: is_valid_review is false (and the event is skipped) if review_id is missing or the rating doesn't parse to 1-5. is_negative_review is true only for 1-3 star reviews.

nodes.name: If Review Is Valid
nodes.notes:
Confirms the payload has a usable review ID and a 1–5 star rating before continuing.

Yes → check for duplicates.
No → route to Skip. This catches malformed Zapier payloads or a misconfigured field mapping — better to skip silently than alert the firm about a review that couldn't be parsed.

nodes.name: Skip Invalid Review Payload
nodes.notes: The incoming payload was missing a review ID or a valid 1–5 star rating — most likely a Zapier field-mapping issue. No alert sent. Check the Zapier zap's action step against the deploy guide's field list if this keeps happening.

nodes.name: Deduplicate By Review ID
nodes.notes:
Prevents the firm from getting alerted twice for the same review.

Uses n8n's built-in workflow static data to remember review_ids it has already processed — no external database or extra API lookup call. Entries older than 30 days are pruned automatically on every run so this never grows unbounded.

Caveat: static data lives on this n8n instance's execution store. If you ever move to queue mode with multiple workers, it does not sync across workers.

Output: is_duplicate (bool).

nodes.name: If Review Is Duplicate
nodes.notes:
Yes (already alerted for this review_id) → Skip, no duplicate alert.
No (first time seeing this review) → continue to the rating check.

nodes.name: Skip Duplicate Review
nodes.notes: This review_id was already processed in the last 30 days — likely a Zapier redelivery or a re-fire from Google after the review was edited. No duplicate alert sent.

nodes.name: If Review Is Negative
nodes.notes:
Google Business Profile reviews use whole-star ratings 1–5 — 'under 4 stars' means 1, 2, or 3.

Yes (1–3 stars) → this is the leak this template plugs → build the instant alert and AI-drafted reply.
No (4–5 stars) → happy review, nothing to do here. Consider pairing this template with the Review Request Engine template, which proactively asks happy clients to leave more reviews like this one.

nodes.name: Skip Positive Review
nodes.notes: This review is 4 or 5 stars — nothing to fix here. Consider pairing this template with the Review Request Engine template, which proactively asks happy clients to leave more reviews like this one.

nodes.name: Prepare Alert And Draft Prompt
nodes.notes:
Builds the instant SMS alert text and the Claude prompt that drafts a safe public reply — the two things this template promises, both within moments of the review landing.

Variables read (project → Variables tab):
  FIRM_NAME — used in the alert and in the Claude prompt
  FIRM_EMAIL / FIRM_FROM_EMAIL — where the full alert + draft email is sent to/from
  FIRM_ALERT_PHONE — the FIRM's own cell number that receives the instant SMS (never the reviewer's number)
  FIRM_TWILIO_NUMBER — your Twilio sending number
  FIRM_GBP_DASHBOARD_URL — fallback link to your Google Business Profile reviews dashboard, used only if Zapier didn't pass a direct review_url

Model: claude-sonnet-4-6, capped at 400 output tokens — replies are short by design. The prompt hard-codes ABA Formal Opinion 496 guardrails: never confirm a client relationship, never reference case facts, never admit fault. Extract And Safety-Check Draft Response re-verifies this with an independent keyword scan.

nodes.name: Send SMS Alert To Firm
nodes.notes:
Texts the FIRM (not the reviewer) the instant heads-up — this is the '24-hour window' trigger the whole template is built around. The full email with the review details and drafted reply follows a few seconds later.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search Twilio → enter Account SID and Auth Token from console.twilio.com → save as 'Twilio account'.

If Twilio isn't configured yet or the send fails, the workflow continues — the follow-up email still delivers the alert and draft, so nothing is lost, just less instant.

nodes.name: Post Draft Review Generation
nodes.notes:
Sends the review to Claude (Anthropic) and receives the drafted public reply as JSON.

Credential: Settings → Credentials → New → search 'Header Auth' → Name: 'Anthropic API key' → Header Name: 'x-api-key' → Header Value: your Anthropic API key from console.anthropic.com.

The anthropic-version header (2023-06-01) is required by the Anthropic API and is added automatically by this node.

Cost: capped at 400 output tokens, well under $0.01 per review. A firm handling a handful of negative reviews a month spends pennies a year on this step.

The JSON Body reads claude_request via an explicit '$("Build Alert And Draft Prompt")' reference rather than $json — the immediately preceding node (Send Instant SMS Alert To Firm) is a Twilio node, which replaces the item's data with its own API response (or an {error: ...} shape when the SMS fails) instead of passing upstream fields through. Reading $json here would silently break whenever the SMS send is skipped or fails.

nodes.name: Parse And Check Draft Response
nodes.notes:
Two-layer safety check before this draft ever reaches the firm's inbox:

Layer 1 — Claude's self-report: if Claude returns is_response_safe: false, the draft is discarded.
Layer 2 — Post-hoc keyword scan: independently scans the draft for language that would confirm a client relationship, reference case facts, or admit fault — the exact things ABA Formal Opinion 496 says a firm cannot do in a public review reply.

is_response_safe is true only if both layers pass. When false, the delivery email tells the firm to write the reply manually instead of using the draft — the instant alert and review details still go out either way.

Also builds the final email subject and body used by Notify Firm Of Negative Review.

nodes.name: Run Compliance Audit Workflow
nodes.notes:
Calls the Bar-Compliance Guardrail to log this negative-review event to your compliance audit sheet.

This workflow alerts your own firm, not a client — so opt-out checking does not apply and approved will always be true here. The purpose of this call is the audit trail: what review triggered an alert, when, and what was drafted.

The guardrail workflow ID is read from the GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID n8n Variable (Settings → Variables). Set it to the numeric ID from the Bar-Compliance Guardrail workflow URL: .../workflow/WORKFLOW_ID.

nodes.name: Send Negative Review Email Notification
nodes.notes:
Delivers the full alert — review details, direct reply link, and the AI-drafted reply (or a note to write it manually if the safety check flagged it) — to your inbox.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search SMTP → enter your email provider's settings → save as 'Email account (SMTP)'.
  Gmail: use an App Password (Google Account → Security → App Passwords)
  Microsoft 365: use your email and password; enable SMTP AUTH in the M365 admin center

This is the second half of the 'instant alert plus a drafted response' promise — the SMS a few nodes back was the instant heads-up; this email has everything needed to act.

All values are read from Extract And Safety-Check Draft Response — not the immediate input — because the guardrail's response has a different data shape than the review/draft details.

body.review_text: Called three times and never got a callback about my case status. Very frustrated with the communication.

description: Alerts the firm within moments of a new Google Business Profile review rated 1-3 stars, then drafts a safe public reply with Claude under ABA Formal Opinion 496 guardrails (never confirms a client relationship, never references case facts, never admits fault) — independently re-checked by a keyword scan before it reaches the firm's inbox. Replaces reputation-management tools ($99-$2,000/mo). Fed by a free Zapier 'New Review' zap; dedupes with n8n's built-in static data, no external database or lookup call. Logs every event to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet.
